title: Shiki
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: In the isolated village of Sotoba in a hot summer of 1994, mysterious deaths spread just as the Kirishiki family moves into a hilltop mansion. Hospital director Toshio Ozaki first suspects an epidemic, then learns the dead are rising as shiki, vampire-like beings. As the shiki take over villagers, Toshio exposes them and the human villagers turn to mass killing, and the village is burned while the priest-novelist Seishin sides with the ancient shiki girl Sunako. Ryu Fujisaki's manga adapts Fuyumi Ono's novel.
life_message: When survival is at stake, both predators and their prey can become monsters; mercy and humanity are easily lost.

content.note: Staking, killings, a village war and burning (Wikipedia); MAL manga reviewers describe gore it does not soften; MangaUpdates Corpses and Sudden Deaths.

Megumi's one-sided crush; no sexual content noted by reviewers.

Seishin's past suicide attempt, Sunako's wish to die and Natsuno's suicide attack (Wikipedia); MangaUpdates Insanity.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Ozaki family reputation matters to Toshio's parents (Wikipedia); villagers answer threats with mob force.

Order vs freedom.evidence: Village follows age-old customs strictly (MangaUpdates blurb); gossip polices Megumi.

Civic vs kin.evidence: Families and village insiders against outsiders.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Hospital and temple families hold standing.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Doctor's science against priest and old customs, both shown failing.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Survival of each species drives everything (AniList Survival).

folkways.japan: Depicts the closed rural Japanese village (mura) with its conformity, gossip and old customs, which the story treats critically.

delivery.evidence: MAL manga reviewers call it ambiguous, leaving the reader to contemplate who is right.

personified.ideology: Protect the village by any means
A predator's right to live though forsaken by God

delivery.note: Both humans and shiki get motives and atrocities, so neither side is reduced to a caricature.

winners_losers: No side wins: the shiki are wiped out, the village burns and Toshio wonders if it was worth it; Seishin and Sunako escape; sympathy is divided.
to_verify: Wikipedia article is for the novel; it notes manga-specific differences, but other details may differ from the manga.
English availability: MangaUpdates lists Shueisha as English publisher with no detail; check license.
